chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Not reading music: Tatum and Slam, and faking a symphony date in Germany
summary: Nobody in the trio read music; he describes learning a score by ear at a rehearsal for Odetta in Germany and Tatum's perfect pitch.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did Tatum know that you didn't read music?

Oh yeah. He didn't read music. Nobody read no music. We had no time for no music. I don't know if Slam could read or not, even. Maybe, I really don't know. I know I didn't. Shit, never crossed my mind to read no music. I have faked it quite a few times. I mean faked it too, I faked it in Germany about 5 years ago or 6 years ago --- This one was with Sonny Payne, we were in Frankfurt not Frankfurt -- right next to Frankfurt... Anyhow it was over there with a 70 piece symphony band with Odetta as star. And 5 bass players, harps. Milt Buckner was there... And they laid out all this music, you know. Well see, they were rehearsing, you know what I mean, they had to rehearse, they had to get Odetta's music together. And 70-piece symphony band. And the funny part about it was it was a little embarassing but I say I didn't care. 'Cause when I opened up my guitar and the german people in the band they started snickering saw these 4 strings they started snickering, ha ha. I say, with hell with them. Let them get their parts. Now they got all this great big sheet of music

About 5 of 'em. Now me like I said, looked like Greek to me. Although this was about six years ago, I could read fairly good, but this was out of sight. So I didn't say anything, I just listened. And they rehearsed all day, for the next day, and by the time they were ready to go to work the next day I had mine, just by listening. I knew exactly what to do -- my little interlude and whatnot. (haha) But this couldn't touch Art Tatum or Slam, they couldn't touch 'em. Those guys, you could blow an automobile horn or tinkle a glass & they could tell you exactly what note it is. Perfect pitch, you know. I couldn't do that. I don't know how they did it. But they would get into arguments. Sometime it would be between the keys, that they would know. But it could hear musically if it was wrong -- you keys playin' it and I'll get it. But there comes a time when they ain't got no time -- listenin' -- and then trouble is there. I managed to get by with it.
